title: Google’s AI note-taking app transcribes your meetings completely offline
slides: Google's offline note app: does it really ignore cloud?
It transcribes meetings on your device without internet.
But how accurate is offline transcription vs cloud?
You can now record sensitive meetings without data leaving.
Test it on a confidential call; check the transcript quality.
thread_text:
1. Offline Transcription Is Here

Google's new note app transcribes meetings on-device without internet. No cloud upload at all.

2. How Accurate Is It?

Offline transcription may drop words or mishear accents compared to cloud. Accuracy trade-off is real.

3. Sensitive Meetings Safe

You can record confidential calls without data leaving your phone. This changes what's possible for privacy.

4. Test on a Real Call

Pick a non-critical confidential call and compare the transcript to what was said. Check for errors.

5. Your Turn to Compare

Take a 5-minute call and run it through the app. Does the quality justify ditching the cloud?

instagram.caption:
Google’s new note app transcribes your meetings entirely on your device, no internet needed. 🔒

Nothing gets uploaded to the cloud, so the audio never leaves your phone.

That matters for anyone recording confidential calls or client conversations. 🎙️

The trade-off: offline transcription may drop words or mishear accents compared to cloud tools.

If you publish content from interviews or calls, this changes what you can safely record. 📱

Pick a 5-minute call, run it through the app, and compare the transcript to what was actually said. ⚖️

Would you ditch the cloud for that quality?
